sources.title: Léo Lelièvre (1899-1966)
sources.creator: Bibliothèque nationale de France; Library of Congress
sources.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF); Library of Congress
sources.researchNote: Two lyricists of the same name were at work in Paris in the 1930s: the chansonnier Léo Lelièvre (1872-1956), born in Reims, and his son Léo Edmond Lelièvre (1899-1966), a member of SACEM from November 1919, who wrote for the Casino de Paris beside Henri Varna and whose covers name him “Léo Lelièvre fils”, among them “Gosse de Paris” (1929) and “Le Tambour-major” from the revue “Paris qui brille” (1931). Both men worked on “Parade de France” in 1934: the Salabert prints of Maïotte Almaby’s créole numbers “La Vraie Créola” and “Ma Goulou Goulou” read “paroles françaises de Léo Lelièvre père”, while the Coda prints of the Jurmann–Kaper songs carry the undifferentiated form. The BnF catalogue is divided over those Coda prints: the notices for the illustrated issues and for the chant-et-piano prints of “C’est chez nous” and “Un baiser de femme sous un ciel de feu” link the son, whereas notices for three further printings of “Un baiser de femme sous un ciel de feu”, including Paul Saegel’s orchestral arrangement, still link the father. The son is preferred on three grounds: the printed “père” used for the other Lelièvre inside the same revue, the continuity of the Varna partnership at the Casino de Paris from 1929 onwards, and the weight of the revised catalogue notices.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Léo Lelièvre (fils)
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Léo Lelièvre (fils).” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Born 9 June 1899 in Paris, died 21 June 1966 in Prague; admitted to SACEM as author on 13 November 1919 and as composer on 21 April 1927, elected full member in 1927; Prix Ferny, 1939. Accessed 25 August 2026.
sources.title: Léo Lelièvre (fils)
sources.creator: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.researchNote: The society through which both men licensed their work distinguishes the son by the qualifier “fils” and dates his membership from 1919, ten years before the first Casino de Paris covers that carry that qualifier. The place of death, Prague, is recorded here alone among the authority files consulted.

sources.shortCitation: “M. Léo Lelièvre fils,” L’Ami du peuple, 12 May 1929
sources.fullCitation: “M. Léo Lelièvre fils.” Portrait photograph by Henri Manuel. L’Ami du peuple (Paris), 12 May 1929, p. 9. RetroNews, Bibliothèque nationale de France. Accessed 25 August 2026.
sources.title: M. Léo Lelièvre fils
sources.creator: Henri Manuel (photographer)
sources.researchNote: The caption reads “M. Léo Lelièvre fils”, so the newspaper itself distinguishes the sitter from his father, the chansonnier Léo Lelièvre (1872-1956). The studio credit “(Photo Henri Manuel)” is printed beneath the image. In 1929 the son was thirty and had been writing for the Casino de Paris beside Henri Varna.

media.title: Léo Lelièvre fils — portrait photograph by Henri Manuel, 1929
media.description: Press portrait of the lyricist Léo Lelièvre fils, printed in the Paris daily L’Ami du peuple on 12 May 1929 with the studio credit “(Photo Henri Manuel)”.
media.altText: Half-length newspaper portrait of Léo Lelièvre fils, turned in profile.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The portrait carries the studio credit of Henri Manuel, who died in 1947, so the seventy-year term of protection in France ran out at the end of 2017; the issue in which it appeared was published in 1929.
media.publicCaption: Portrait of the lyricist Léo Lelièvre fils, published in L’Ami du peuple on 12 May 1929.
